newsitem.title: UK: British stocks pin hopes on prudent budget.
newsitem.headline: British stocks pin hopes on prudent budget.

text.p: Britain's stockmarket will focus on Tuesday's budget and the reaction of bond and currency markets with investors hoping for a prudent plan to put the London equity market back on track.

The stockmarket has been characterised by cautious trade and unwilling to make progress despite a supportive gilts market amid fears over rising interest rates since an unexpected 1/4 point rise in base rates last month.

But market players are increasingly hopeful that the Chancellor will resist the temptation to woo the electorate with potentially inflationary tax cuts which will increase the danger of monetary tightening.
Traders say net tax cuts of around two billion pounds, equivalent to a penny off the basic rate of tax, have already been discounted but signs of more generous give-aways could raise concern.

On Friday, the UK's leading blue-chip index managed to shake off its lethargy to close up 64.9 points or 1.64 percent at 4018.7 as worries over interest rates and the budget were pushed to the background.
But strategists say the need for another pre-election interest rate rise cannot be ignored.

"Given the underlying strength of the economy and disappointing inflation data, we are braced for further base rate rises," said Panmure Gordon's Stuart Weatherby. "A cautious budget would reduce the urgency but we still expect one more increase before the general election."

Chancellor Clarke's strategy for ensuring the economy remains healthy will determine overall sentiment next week but individual sectors will be watching for specific budget measures relating to their businesses.

"The recent ruling on tax credits on share buybacks and special dividends underlined how the Treasury is currently thinking," Weatherby warned. "The corporate sector is likely to bear the brunt of revenue-raising measures."
Other scheduled economic news for the week ahead is sparse but will include global trade statistics on Wednesday and money supply and credit data on Friday.
Among companies reporting next week National Grid and Severn Trent are due to post results on budget day. The utilities sector will be watching for windfall tax raising measures on Tuesday as well.
British Biotech and Tate & Lyle report on Wednesday followed by British Gas, Royal Bank of Scotland, Southern Electric and United Utilities on Thursday. Friday sees results from Yorkshire Water.
